title: The Courage of Stephen
english: Then we cry out with the army of Israel and sing victory songs as if seeing them present, marveling as if they were standing.

For every one who fights for piety is good, even if he becomes second or third to those who competed before; yet he is not worthy of such a marvel as the first. The second, being stirred by zeal for the one who preceded, was thus drawn toward diligence; but he who uses no one as a guide, yet having become a discoverer of the good, appropriately receives the vote of the first.

Great indeed is the man's readiness, therefore great is the honor; and immortal is the memory, which neither oblivion covered nor time dimmed, but generation after generation, inheriting the stories, we priests, people, children, men, and women, celebrate this feast without fail. But the history itself should also be observed, so that, having become acquainted with the facts of the matters, we might more marvel at the man.

First among those who serve according to Christ was Stephen, esteemed by grace, a vessel filled with the Spirit, confirming daily those in the household and those wandering toward the straight path. And because he had a more intense teaching, he more than the other apostles loosed the enemies and, before them, first made the devil hostile. For he sets his eyes like fire and looks fiercely at those who are more steadfast in piety. Thus the race of Alexandrians raised up a sharp-edged system against him for a stand. In any case, you have heard of the men of the city, how they are both fervent and boiling upon everything they might readily rush toward. And when the crowd saw those rushing toward him, it had almost been possible to set the present situation aside; however, he found a resourceful, well-composed, and gentle word. For there is no medicine of such a kind for the healing of temper and agitation, such as a pleasant and well-fitted exhortation.

And 'tell me,' he says, 'the cause of the hatred, instead of why you stretch out your hands and are manifest as if about to strike.' When it was said that 'Since you destroy the ancestral laws and are an introducer of foreign dogmas,' the blessed one stood in the midst; for as an unskilled and impromptu orator, he was saying what he had learned from art, but what was breathed into him by the Spirit: 'Men,' he says, 'brothers and fathers.'

Listen. The introduction is wise, an excellent thing for the people being warmed by it, the beginning of the oration. For the sweetness and the appropriateness of the words, as if participating in some honey or soft oil, diminished the heat of the beasts. Then he rises in memory toward Abraham, so that having begun from ancient times and stretching out a long discourse in much of the middle, he might not be found to have spent his spirit being exhausted. And having worked out that much speech, he shows that even Moses prophesied Christ, so that through the reliability of the lawgiver, skillfully, like a thief, he might introduce the word of faith. And he has said all things knowing, all that was useful for the benefit of those listening.

But when he saw the evil to be unprovable and the opinion unyielding, then he was filled with boldness and, forbidding all the flattering art toward the life here, he unhesitatingly reproved them: stiff-necked, uncircumcised in heart, fighting against the law, warring against the Spirit. And what [things] from here? Many dogs and fattened bulls stood around him as a Master, as the psalmody says, surrounding the righteous man (Psalm 22:2). But he stood alone, surrounded on every side by the people of the murderers. And no one was near at that hour, no friend, no householder, no relative. For it is as if one offers a consolation to those in danger by seeing someone known nearby.

But the high champion of the great struggle, having seen the need for a man to stand by, for he was very brave, shows that he suffered all human things unceasingly; as it seems to him, gazing intently toward heaven (Acts 7:55), he shows also the Son standing at the right hand in the form of humanity (Acts 7:56). O, the philanthropy! O, the goodness! To the athlete, those for which he struggled appeared, and the God of all things did not leave such a voice to him alone. Do not suffer anything ungentle, O Stephen; you have no human ally, no friend stood by you in the time of terrors, but I, with the Beloved, watch over the things being done. Rest is ready, the gates of paradise having been opened. Having endured a little, leave behind a brief life and hasten toward the life which is eternal and perfect. Still finding yourself in the flesh, you see God, a thing of all the world.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Martyrdom and Prayer of Christ-bearer
english: You were initiated by the more prominent apostles into the truth that the Father has a genuine, beloved Son. I show myself to you so that you may be able to bear the burden. And the Son stood by my side, so that you might know his honor by the relation of place. At that time, many were scandalized that God had clothed himself in flesh on earth; but see him now in the heights, with me, bearing the form of man in the heavenly and hyper-heavenly realms, as a confirmation of the completed economy. Do not be crushed or grow limp by being overwhelmed by this.

Looking at the athlete, do not be afraid of the contest. Do not despise the body, treating it as an earthly bond, a fragile house, or a corrupt vessel of a potter. Ascend toward the end here in freedom, for the crown of manliness is ready for you. Transfer from the earth to heaven. Leave the body to the scavengers like food for dogs. Leave behind a raging people and come to the dance of angels.

After this resolve, God appeared to the patient one, so that he might not suffer something cowardly, and might release much eagerness through the greatness of fear. Therefore, God neither sent him an angel as a helper, as he later did for the apostles in prison (Acts 12:5), nor any ministerial and fellow-servant power, but he manifested himself. For it was then the firstfruits of the testimony, and it was necessary for the first work to be completed, so that those following, being built up as witnesses, might receive a strong foundation of zeal and not become imitators of cowardice, which is exactly what happens in common wars. For one soldier, a champion, providing the glorious part of the work, having conquered and having emboldened all his own, strikes down the opponents; yet, having suffered a slight injury, he immediately collapses and fills the souls of his kinsmen with cowardice, and flight becomes a habit. For this reason, God appeared from heaven.

But he who was worthy of the great vision did not hold in silence what he saw, but immediately cried out: 'Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!' (Rev 4:1). For he thought that the revealing of the vision would draw the unbelievers into agreement. But those making the spoken word a starting point for greater wrath and madness, attempting to block...

They held their ears against the word as if it were blasphemy, immediately ready for death. Dragging the Christ-bearing man outside the city, bearing his endurance as the Lord bore the cross, they return evil for evil and justify murder with murder, and with stones they bind the one who serves the cornerstone.

Standing him on a certain level field, that long body and high trophy of the martyrs, the mob of blood and wrath surrounded him, and imitating the sling used in wars, they threw stones at the servant of the cornerstone, and every Hebrew hand enacted the murder; the aim was for those leaving that the martyr stood in the middle like a target for an archer.

As the body was shattered from every side and smeared with blood, it rushed toward the upright position; it leaned and threatened to fall like a tall plane tree being worked on by many carpenters; but it did not suffer an improper fall according to the many. For it was not cast headlong, nor was it thrown on its side, nor was the form reclined upon its back, but having set its knees in the proper form of one praying, it descended, hastening with the soul through prayer the separation from the flesh and crying out to the visible Lord: 'Lord Jesus Christ, receive my spirit.'

For he was hastening as if to some migration, as if from a foreign land to a fatherland, as if to a bright city from a desert and smoky land. And he added to his petition the prayer for those throwing stones. For those blessing and those stoning were saving, and those murdering were making alive, and those separating from the clay were sending to the kingdom.

Let us therefore consider also the word of the prayer, regarding toward what end it carries 'Lord, do not hold their sin against them' (Luke 23:34). For it is not, as some wickedly thinking men suppose, that the sin of the enemies becomes unpunished and unaccountable. For this was clearly to stand against God's decree and to restore the judgment and law of the righteous, having completed what was due to the murderers.
But what does he say? 'Lord, do not hold their sin against them,' that is: Give the fear of compunction, lead to repentance those now having dared,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Presence of the Spirit in Stephen
english: Do not allow yourself to die in circumcision; draw through repentance toward your own recognition, and kindle in the hearts the flame of the Spirit. For if they are improved in this way, it is evident that you will not stand against their sin, but having washed in the bath of grace, both your blood and mine, they will become free from the accusations.

These things happened and the drama was completed. And the armies of angels were rejoicing in the contest, marveling greatly and with much retinue leading Stephen into his own inheritance; but the devil was turned away empty, being terribly perplexed, but in order to imitate a prophetic word concerning the airy spirit, saying something more bodily, as one carrying the face of a pot as a vessel and, on the contrary to what he expected, having succeeded in those by which he thought to diminish Christians, through those he increased the list of the martyrs.

And what also toward Paul is the temple? For he too was one of the murderers, a true Benjamin, a wolf having snatched the lamb. For if he himself did not stone, but kept the garments of those stoning and served the people's crowd. Moreover, I shall see you soon, now trembling and breathing a wild passion like a weak old woman being led about, when you are about to be led toward the Ananias of the truth, having tasted it.

And I shall laugh very much when I hear you recounting your tribulations for the sake of the gospel and, among the other dangers, saying: 'At last I was stoned.' For it is necessary for you to defend yourself through stones against the stones, and by the same suffering to loose the accusation of sin.

It is also unbearable not to leave the vision of Stephen behind; for the God of all things always, foreseeing what is about to happen to the lives of sinful men, provides the remedy defensively in advance, which indeed He has done even here. For if the theophanies were completed only for the benefit of the combatant, it would have sufficed to become a voice from the heavens, just as at the baptism before, or later at the transfiguration, or even as with this Paul, when he was traveling toward Damascus.
Now, because the evil from Libya is about to lie in wait for the churches of God, and the ill-famed confusion of the hypotheses...

To lead into life, for this reason God, as if cutting ahead in advance and securing the souls of those who are to come later, shows himself to Stephen in a private and self-sufficient glory, and shows the Son in a perfected appearance, and places him at his own right hand, so that through the clarity of the persons he might interpret the underlying realities.

12.13.1 And someone might happen to say: The things concerning the Father and the Son are thus philosophized for you, but where is the Holy Spirit? For if, for the sake of the security according to faith, the Father was appearing from heaven with the Son, it was necessary for the Holy Spirit also to be present, so that some practical initiation might be accomplished for men through the vision. It is therefore necessary to say to the mind bearing this against us: O most wise, the examiner of readers must have both a correct mind and a strengthened memory, so that he may be able thus to run through all the written things together.

12.13.2 For if you also seek the presence of the Spirit, become a little higher than the stones and the marble, and you will find before the vision the Spirit speaking and being present with Stephen and preparing the athlete. For immediately at the beginning of the narrative he pre-announced this voice to us: 'Stephen, full of grace and truth, was doing signs and great wonders among the people' (Acts 6:8). And some rose up from the assembly called the Libertines and the Cyrenians and the Alexandrians and those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen, and they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the spirit with which he was speaking (Acts 6:9-10).

12.13.3 Behold, then, also the person of the Spirit has been made clear to us by the word. If this was written earlier, and the Father and the Son last, the faith is not deprived of anything regarding the order. For it is the custom of the Scripture to do this: sometimes naming the Son alone, sometimes the Spirit with the Son, or sometimes beginning from the Father and concluding in the Spirit; and the repetition of the beginning occurring from the Spirit through the Son, the word leads back to the Father.
12.13.4 And this idiom of custom is seen to be happening most without concealment by the great Paul. And it has been filled among us
